The new README code-map row says without qualification that close ends the whole browser process group. The package's own close() can resolve with the group still alive: after 3 x graceMs, when the OS refuses the signal, it gives up and writes one stderr line. The test 'never hangs' asserts the browser is still alive after close. Because the browser runs detached, a crash or kill -9 of the owner also leaves the group running. Spec §3 promises no orphans after kill -9, and that rests on a K4 sweep that does not exist yet. A reader of the map takes close as the whole guarantee. (docs/README.md:106, found by the `product` tier)

The runbook says gates do not fail on the clock under heavy machine load, and that a timeout failure means a hang, not a slow machine. pipe.test.ts now has wall-clock upper bounds on real child processes: under 3 x 200 + 50 ms in 'never hangs', and under 2500 ms in 'asks first'. A slow machine can fail those without anything hanging. Measured: 5 of 5 runs passed with 28 busy loops on 14 cores, so the window is narrow but real. (docs/runbooks/development.md:259-261; packages/cdp-pipe/src/pipe.test.ts:178,232, found by the `product` tier)
